title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page (5) of a sequence (pages 5-23 per the previous page). Grothendieck builds a finite, highly symmetric presentation of the fundamental groupoid of the projective line minus 0, 1, ∞ (that is, M_{0,4}, or Σ^× in his notation). He then studies automorphisms compatible with its symmetries. This is the set-up from which, on the next page, he extracts Drinfeld-type Grothendieck–Teichmüller equations.

1. Figure and data. Each cusp i ∈ {0, 1, ∞} carries two base points R_i^ω and R_i^{ω'}. They are best read as the two real tangential base points at i, or as base points in the upper and lower half-planes indexed by the primitive cube roots of unity ω, ω'. That gives six base points.
- The a_i^ω : R_i^ω → R_i^{ω'} are half-loops around cusp i. Composing the two half-loops at a cusp gives a full loop: a_i^{ω'} a_i^ω = λ_i^ω, the inertia loop at i (relation (3)).
- The b_i^ω : R_{ωi}^ω → R_{ω'i}^{ω'} are the paths along the three real segments joining neighbouring cusps. Here the index i is shifted by the cyclic action of ω on {0, 1, ∞}.

2. Symmetries.
- The group G_T acts simply transitively on the six a's and on the six b's. It is the order-6 group S_3 of automorphisms of P^1 permuting {0, 1, ∞}, i.e. the anharmonic group.
- Complex conjugation τ (the I_T margin note) acts by τ(R_i^ω) = R_i^{ω'} and τ(a_i^ω) = (a_i^{ω'})^{-1}, and by a formula for τ(b_i^ω) that is hard to read.

3. Relations (2).
- (2a) b_i^ω b_i^{ω'} = 1. Going along a real segment and back is trivial; this gives three relations.
- (2b) An alternating hexagon a b a b a b = 1 around each hemisphere. This gives two effective relations, one for each ω in the underlined ω (= {ω, ω'}).
- So the 6-vertex groupoid is presented by the a's and b's subject to the 2-cycle and hexagon relations, with S_3 × ⟨τ⟩ symmetry.

4. Model group. Relation (4) gives, for each base point, an isomorphism φ_i^ω from the model group Π_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3}, R_0^+) = ⟨ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ | ℓ_∞ ℓ_1 ℓ_0 = 1⟩ (free on two generators) to π_1(Σ^×, R_i^ω).
- It sends ℓ_0 ↦ a_i^{ω'} a_i^ω, and ℓ_1 to an explicit conjugate built from b's and a's.
- Π_{0,3} is embedded in an extended group Π̃_{0,3} = π_1(M_{0,3}, G_3; R_0^+), an orbifold/semi-direct extension by the symmetry group. This extension contains the automorphisms τ_∞, σ_∞, ε_0 and ρ.
- The φ_i^ω are permuted simply transitively by the transition maps.

5. Transport formulas (5), (6), (9).
- (5) Conjugation corresponds to τ_∞: ℓ_0 ↦ ℓ_0^{-1}, ℓ_1 ↦ ℓ_1^{-1}, ℓ_∞ ↦ ℓ_0 ℓ_1 = int(ℓ_0) ℓ_∞^{-1}.
- (6) Transport along a_i corresponds to ε_0, a square root of ℓ_0 (half-twist, ε_0^2 = ℓ_0). Transport along b_i corresponds to σ_∞: ℓ_0 ↔ ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ ↦ (ℓ_0 ℓ_1)^{-1} = int(ℓ_0) ℓ_∞. This is the involution z ↦ 1 - z.
- (7) He introduces the composite b̃_i^ω = a_{ω'i}^{ω'} b_i^ω, a real segment followed by a half-turn.
- (8)/(9) In terms of b̃, the hexagon (2b) becomes the 3-cycle relation b̃_{ω²i} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i = 1. Transport along b̃ corresponds to ρ^{-1} = ε_0 σ_∞, where ρ is the order-3 rotation ℓ_0 → ℓ_1 → ℓ_∞ → ℓ_0.
- A marginal NB observes that one of the b̃ is not τ-stable, so one should also take the τ b̃_i.

6. Purpose. This is the level-1 (M_{0,4}) piece of the 'Teichmüller tower' programme of the Esquisse. On the next page, an automorphism u commuting with G_T and preserving the sub-groupoids generated by the a's and b̃'s is written as:
- u(a) = a φ(ℓ_0^γ), with ρ ∈ Ẑ^* (a multiplier) and γ = (ρ - 1)/2;
- u(b̃) = b̃ φ(β), with β ∈ π̂_{0,3}.
Relations (2a) and (8) then translate into β σ_∞(β) = 1 and α ρ^{-1}(α) ρ^{-2}(α) = 1, with α = ℓ_1^γ β. These are exactly Drinfeld's GT relations (I) and (II), f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 and the hexagon with m = (λ - 1)/2. They are obtained here via a symmetric 6-base-point groupoid with S_3 × ⟨τ⟩ symmetry.
errors: Index bookkeeping in (2b) as written (a_i^ω b_{ωi}^ω a_i^{ω'} b_{ωi}^ω a_{ω'i}^{ω'} b_i^ω) is garbled. For the hexagon to close, the a's must sit at three different cusps (indices i, ωi, ω²i), as is consistent with (7)-(8).
Line (8) is first written with repeated index b̃_{ωi} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i. It is corrected at the bottom of the page to b̃_{ω²i} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i = 1.
The target of b̃_i^ω in (7) is written ambiguously and partly crossed out. With b_i^ω : R_{ωi}^ω → R_{ω'i}^{ω'} followed by a_{ω'i}^{ω'}, the target is R_{ω'i}^{ω}, not R_{ωi}^{ω}.

Formulas (5) and (6) for τ_∞ and σ_∞ check out: they respect ℓ_∞ ℓ_1 ℓ_0 = 1, and the int(ℓ_0) rewritings are correct. ρ also preserves the relation up to conjugacy. The identity ρ^{-1} = ε_0 σ_∞ only holds up to inner automorphisms and depends on the precise definition of ε_0, which is not written out. No substantive error otherwise.

ideas.what: Presentation of π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}) as a groupoid on 6 symmetric base points, generated by half-turns a_i at the cusps and real-segment paths b_i, with relations b b' = 1 and an alternating hexagon a b a b a b = 1
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with real tangential base points; the 'Lego'/Teichmüller groupoid of M_{0,4} with S_3 symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Drinfeld (1990); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps / Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for a,b presentations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and its two-level generation, without explicit formulas

ideas.what: Model group Π_{0,3} with an extension Π̃_{0,3} containing the involution σ_∞, the 3-cycle ρ, the half-twist ε_0 (ε_0² = ℓ_0) and the conjugation τ_∞; transports along the a's and b's identified with ε_0 and σ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Action of the anharmonic group S_3 (and complex conjugation) on F̂_2; orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,4}/S_3

ideas.what: Rewriting the hexagon as a 3-cycle relation b̃_{ω²i} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i = 1 via b̃ = a b, so that b̃ transports by ρ^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Passage from the hexagon relation to the 3-cycle relation (II) of GT

ideas.what: Systematic inclusion of complex conjugation τ as an extra symmetry of the groupoid (τ(a) = a'^{-1}), anticipating the λ = -1 element of GT
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation as an element of GT (λ = -1, f = 1)

missed.claim: This page sets up the groupoid computation which, on the next page, yields exactly Drinfeld's defining equations of GT: f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1, and the hexagon with m = (λ - 1)/2. The archive dating is 'à partir de 1978', i.e. plausibly before Drinfeld 1990. The derivation goes through a 6-base-point groupoid with S_3 × ⟨τ⟩ symmetry, a presentation equivalent to the later Lochak–Schneps and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps a,b formalism.
missed.quote: Les relations (2b) deviennent b̃_{ω²i} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the explicit level-1 GT relations, not only the Esquisse philosophy. Historians and GT specialists generally credit the equations to Drinfeld and Ihara.

missed.claim: The marginal remark that one of the b̃_i is not τ-stable, so one should use the τ-images, flags an unresolved choice of τ-symmetric normalisation. The next page likewise asks for a direct check that the equations are stable under β ↦ σ_∞(β).
missed.quote: L'une des b̃_i^ω n'est pas stable sous τ il faudrait donc prendre les τ b̃_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It concerns choosing τ-equivariant normalisations of GT parameters (cf. real structures and GT^± variants). The verification itself is easy.

deep.surprise_reason: It is widely 'known' that Grothendieck anticipated GT. Seeing him explicitly build the symmetric 6-base-point groupoid and convert the hexagon into the 3-cycle relation, en route to equations identical to Drinfeld's, is a notable concrete detail. However, the content is now standard, and the archive material has been studied by specialists such as Schneps, so it is not shocking.
transcription_corrections: 'G_T permet transitivement' should read 'G_T permute transitivement les six flèches a_i^ω et les six flèches b_i^ω'.
In (2a), the parenthetical reads '(trois relations effectives)' with 'effectives' struck through.
In (2b), the note reads 'deux relations effectives, une pour chaque ω ∈ ω̲' (underlined ω = {ω, ω'}).
Σ^× in (4) is the punctured sphere P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Π̃_{0,3} = π_1(M_{0,3}, G_3; R_0^+) seems to denote the extended (orbifold) group.
Line (8)/(10) should be b̃_{ω²i} b̃_{ωi} b̃_i = 1. The final line's label is struck through and 'Les relations (2b) deviennent' is the intended text.
The marginal NB reads: 'L'une des b̃_i^ω n'est pas stable sous τ, il faudrait donc aussi prendre les τ b̃_i^ω'.
